claims.text: The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films are governed primarily by nanoscale chemical ordering and associated local lattice distortions.
The nanoscale chemical ordering and local lattice distortions result from substrate-induced strain during film deposition.
Substrate-induced strain stabilizes a metastable ordered phase responsible for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films have a predominantly hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited films contain subtle nanoscale chemical inhomogeneities.
The as-deposited films retain residual strain from deposition.
Selecting substrates with different lattice mismatches will systematically tune strain during film growth.
Differences in substrate-induced strain affect the degree and uniformity of local chemical ordering.
Enhanced substrate-induced strain promotes a more homogeneous or well-defined ordered state.
A more homogeneous or well-defined ordered state lowers the energy barriers for the magnetostructural transition.
Lower magnetostructural-transition energy barriers reduce hysteresis.
Changes in strain and ordering may shift the magnetostructural transition temperature.
Lower substrate-induced strain retains greater chemical inhomogeneity.
Greater chemical inhomogeneity reinforces a large, sharp entropy change with pronounced hysteresis.
Films on substrates with greater lattice mismatch will exhibit a measurable transition-temperature shift relative to films on the standard substrate.
Films on substrates with greater lattice mismatch will exhibit reduced hysteretic losses relative to the baseline.
Reduced hysteretic losses will be manifested as a broader or less steep transition.
The baseline film on a minimally mismatched standard substrate has a single-phase hexagonal structure, a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition, and significant hysteresis.
The predicted effects should be significant only in sufficiently thin films where substrate-induced strain and substrate coupling are maintained.
The hypothesis may cease to apply in bulk material or after thermal treatment because strain relaxation dominates or the treatment relieves strain.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires both a hysteresis reduction and a transition-temperature shift, whereas the falsification rule treats failure to observe either one as falsifying. This makes the required decisive outcome ambiguous if only one response changes.
